body:
### Unaggregated fills fail details lookup **High Severity** Turning Aggregated off rebuilds trade rows with per-fill ids, but Activity Details still rematches through `usePerpsActivityQuery` with `aggregateFills` defaulting to true. Those ids do not line up with the collapsed order row, so tapping an individual execution opens a not-found details screen, or in the first-row collision case shows the combined order instead of that fill.
Additional Locations (1) - [`app/components/Views/ActivityScreen/ActivityScreen.tsx#L263-L367`](https://github.com/MetaMask/metamask-mobile/blob/96df0045900e5bc7bf05a2644cb6f3dabb6bd4bd/app/components/Views/ActivityScreen/ActivityScreen.tsx#L263-L367)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 96df0045900e5bc7bf05a2644cb6f3dabb6bd4bd. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

Fixed in a23bb80115. Confirmed real: `usePerpsDetailsItem` calls `usePerpsActivityQuery` without the third argument, so it rebuilt the list with `aggregateFills` defaulting to true. A row id minted while the control was off is keyed on the individual fill and does not exist in that aggregated set, so the details screen came up empty.

Details now resolves against both views — aggregated first, then unaggregated — rather than depending on which state the list happened to be in. Both calls share one react-query cache entry (same `queryKey`), so the cost is a second memo, not a second fetch.

Two tests added, and I verified the first fails without the fix (`1 failed, 10 passed`): a row id that only exists while aggregation is off resolves, and the aggregated row still wins when an id is present in both.

### Individual fill opens aggregated details **Medium Severity** Resolving against the aggregated list first can open the combined order when the user tapped a single execution. Both views build ids as `orderId-timestamp-index`, so the newest fill of the newest order always shares the aggregated row id and shows combined size, fees, and PnL.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit a23bb8011507d9dad907b24d9c986f5d4f656a8c. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

Fixed in 707e36971e. Confirmed the collision: aggregated `order-A-1700000002000-0` (5 BTC) and the individual newest fill produced the same id, because an aggregated row carries its last fill's orderId and timestamp. Unaggregated rows now get a `fill-` id namespace, so a tapped id maps to exactly one row and resolution order no longer matters. Test added and verified to fail without it; the earlier test that asserted aggregated-wins was wrong and is removed.

Could we remove this deduplication or key it by a provider supplied execution ID? Hyperliquid identifies each execution with the unique `tid`; `orderId + timestamp + size + price` is not documented as unique. With `aggregateByTime: false`, two legitimate fills can share those four values, and this branch now drops one before either individual display or aggregation, understating execution count, size, fee, and PnL. `origin/main` transforms the fetched fills directly, so this data loss is introduced by `flattenFills`. Please add a regression test with two same-order, same-millisecond, same price, same size fills and verify both remain represented.

Could we base unaggregated row IDs on a stable provider execution identifier rather than `acc.length`? Adding a newer fill shifts the index of every existing row, so a refresh changes FlashList keys and can make the identifier passed to Activity Details resolve to no fill or the wrong fill. Hyperliquid exposes `tid` specifically as the unique trade ID; if the provider-neutral `OrderFill` model cannot carry it yet, we need a stable provider neutral execution ID before exposing individual fills. Please cover the case where a newer fill is prepended and existing execution IDs remain unchanged.

Could we build this control with the existing `Checkbox` from `@metamask/design-system-react-native` so the interactive node has `accessibilityRole="checkbox"`? `ButtonBase` exposes button semantics, while React Native’s `checked` state is defined for checkbox/radio roles; setting only `accessibilityState.checked` does not give assistive technology the checkbox contract. The current tests assert the raw prop but not the role. Please use the design-system primitive and assert both role and checked state.

Suggestion: replace the third positional boolean with an options object and an explicit mode such as `fillDisplay: 'aggregated' | 'individual'`. Calls such as `usePerpsActivityQuery(accountId, enabled, false)` hide the meaning at the call site and allow future invalid boolean combinations. A named options type makes the state space explicit and follows TypeScript’s preference for inference friendly object APIs and modeled domain states.
